claims.claim: Initial reports of blocked property are due within 10 business days from the date that property becomes blocked
An annual report on all blocked property held as of June 30 shall be filed by September 30
Annual report values are stated in U.S. dollars as of June 30, and if a June 30 value date is unavailable the report must so indicate

Reports of blocked property that is unblocked or transferred are due within 10 business days, subject to four enumerated exceptions (authorized service-charge debits; intra-institution transfers between blocked accounts; license-authorized unblocking or transfer unless the license requires a separate report; unblocking upon OFAC removal from the SDN List)

Initial and annual blocked-property reports must be filed electronically through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS); unblocking/transfer reports by email to OFACReport@treasury.gov or through ORS; requests to file by alternative means carry a presumption of denial and must be granted in writing
Reports of rejected transactions are due within 10 business days of the rejected transaction and are submitted through the OFAC Reporting System

Any U.S. person holding, unblocking, or transferring blocked property must report, including financial institutions that receive and block payments; primary responsibility rests with the actual holder, transferrer, or releaser; another person's report does not excuse filing absent actual knowledge of it

A rejected-transaction report is required when a transaction that is not blocked would nonetheless violate a sanctions provision if processed; 'transaction' includes wire transfers, trade finance, securities transactions, checks, foreign exchange, and sales or purchases of goods or services

The legal authority cited in a blocked-property report may be a sanctions program, a CFR part (e.g., 31 CFR part 515 or 544), an Executive order (e.g., E.O. 13224, E.O. 13599), or a statute; the generic term 'SDN' alone is not sufficient
Blocked property with a negative balance (outstanding loans, credit card receivables) is reported as $0.00 with the amount owed described in the narrative
